requirements.statement: Home shows every saved search with how many markets it covers, and opens it on a tap.
requirements.title: List the saved searches

requirements.statement:
A saved search can be edited — vehicle searches in the vehicle form, others in the add sheet — or
deleted.
requirements.title: Edit or delete a saved search

requirements.statement:
A saved search shows when it last found something new, and how much of it, so opening it is a choice
rather than a check.
requirements.title: Say what a saved search has found since last time

requirements.statement: Saved searches are re-run every six hours and alert on new stock or a price well under the median; Home shows whether a search is watched, when it last ran and what it found.
requirements.title: Show that background watching is on

requirements.statement:
Typing a term and confirming asks every market the search covers, translated per country where the
market's own language differs.
requirements.title: Search every market for what was typed

requirements.statement: Products from the catalogue appear under what is being typed and can be searched directly.
requirements.title: Offer catalogue matches while typing

requirements.statement:
A search started from a category tile covers 5 vehicle markets; the same search typed as text covers
25. Both are called every market and nothing says the tile is narrower.
requirements.title: One notion of every market

requirements.statement: A search also covers what the market itself calls the thing, taken from the related searches Kleinanzeigen prints and confirmed against what those searches return. On, on the server.
requirements.title: Search the market's own words for the thing

requirements.statement: Photo, title, price, market, place and age of the ad — enough to judge an offer without opening it.
requirements.title: Show each offer with what decides it

requirements.statement:
While markets are still answering, a thin line says so and removes itself. Results appear as they
arrive rather than at the end.
requirements.title: Show progress without holding the screen

requirements.statement:
The canvas carries the cheapest and nothing else; median, spread, distribution and the New/Used
split move behind a tap, because three summaries of one question is three answers.
requirements.title: One price figure on the canvas

requirements.statement: The count on screen counts what is on screen. Where the filters hide something, that is said in words beside the list rather than as a second number that disagrees with the first.
requirements.title: One count, meaning one thing

requirements.statement:
Each offer that carries a place shows how far it is, measured on the device from the search's own
location, and nearest-first sorts what is already fetched rather than searching again.
requirements.title: Show distance and sort by it

requirements.statement: Two markets of thirty-seven publish when an ad was posted. Newest-first orders by that date rather than by when this app fetched it, the offers no market dated are marked as such where the dated ones stop, and the Markets view names which cannot say.
requirements.title: Show how long the ad has been up

requirements.statement:
Blocking a word hides every offer whose title carries it, matching whole words regardless of
punctuation, and the block is kept with the saved search.
requirements.title: Block a word for good

requirements.statement: An offer can be hidden for good, kept on this device.
requirements.title: Dismiss a single offer

requirements.statement:
The price band set on the results survives closing the view, for every kind of search rather than
only vehicles.
requirements.title: Keep the price band

requirements.statement: Sort order and the New/Used choice are forgotten as soon as the view closes.
requirements.title: Keep the sort order and the condition

requirements.statement:
Results hidden by the filters must read differently from a search that found nothing, and offer the
way back out.
requirements.title: Distinguish nothing found from nothing admitted

requirements.statement:
Price band, markets, countries, blocked words and sort order are set in one place that is opened
from the results and closed back onto them, instead of being laid out across the canvas and the
search form.
requirements.title: Filters live in their own sheet

requirements.statement: Markets are grouped under the country their listings are in, and the country selects every market in it. Both are kept with the search.
requirements.title: Filter by country

requirements.statement:
Market chips filter what was already fetched and the search form re-runs the search. Both are called
filtering and nothing on screen distinguishes them.
requirements.title: Say whether a filter re-asks the markets

requirements.statement:
Per market: the term sent, how many results came back before filtering, how many survived, and what
went wrong. The server holds all of it and the app shows none of it.
requirements.title: Say what each market answered

requirements.statement:
The server tells the app twelve kinds of failure and the app shows four, so blocked, rate limited
and simply empty all look the same.
requirements.title: Distinguish the kinds of failure

requirements.statement: A market cooling down after a block says so, with how long is left, so a search that excludes it does not look complete.
requirements.title: Say which markets are cooling down

requirements.statement:
Eleven markets of thirty-seven turn criteria into their own URL; the rest are filtered over what the
fetched pages happened to contain, which is a weaker guarantee and reads identically.
requirements.title: Say which filters the market itself applied

requirements.statement: The app offers only markets a crawler exists for, taken from the server rather than from a list held here that can fall out of step.
requirements.title: Do not offer a market that cannot be searched

requirements.statement: Every market with a working crawler is offered, including Geizhals and ImmoScout24, because the list comes from the crawlers themselves.
requirements.title: Offer every market that works

requirements.statement: Median, spread and distribution, on their own screen rather than on the results canvas.
requirements.title: Show where a price sits

requirements.statement:
Sold listings are what make a price history real, and only the five eBay markets publish them, so
this is thin or empty everywhere else and must say so.
requirements.title: Show what actually sold

requirements.statement:
Make and model come from a catalogue synced from the sites themselves, so each market is asked in
the token it recognises.
requirements.title: Pick make and model from the sites' own catalogue

requirements.statement:
Year, mileage, price, power, gearbox, fuel, body, condition, drivetrain, doors, seats, emission
class, seller, van length and height, and colour.
requirements.title: Take the criteria a vehicle search needs

requirements.statement:
A free-text description of the ideal vehicle orders the results instead of excluding any, since a
sentence is not a criterion.
requirements.title: Rank by a description rather than filter by it

requirements.statement:
Items given away near the set area are shown one at a time with how well they fit, and swiping
teaches the model.
requirements.title: One item at a time, scored

requirements.statement: The server address is set here and can be tested from here.
requirements.title: Point the app at a server

requirements.statement: The display currency is held in memory and never written, so it is forgotten on restart.
requirements.title: Keep the chosen currency

requirements.statement: Settings are grouped into this device and this server, and the shared group says it is shared, because search depth and the alert settings change them for every client of that server.
requirements.title: Device settings must not be server settings

requirements.statement: Nothing but one title line, one progress line and one row of three controls stands between opening the view and the first offer.
requirements.title: The first screen is offers

requirements.statement: Filters, Price and Markets each carry their own summary — how many filters are active, the best price, how many markets answered — and each opens the view that owns it.
requirements.title: One row of three doors

requirements.statement: Price band, condition, sort order, the chosen markets and countries, and the blocked words are all kept with the search, for every kind of search, not only vehicles.
requirements.title: Every filter survives the view closing

requirements.statement: Changing a filter re-reads what was already fetched. Only a change that no fetched result can answer says so, and asks.
requirements.title: Narrowing does not re-ask the markets

requirements.statement: Each of the server's failure kinds reaches the app as itself, and a market that was blocked, rate limited or timed out is named as such.
requirements.title: A blocked market never reads as an empty one

requirements.statement: The server already reports that a market had further pages and whether the answer came from cache. Neither reaches the app, so a truncated answer looks complete.
requirements.title: Say when a market held more

requirements.statement: Make, model, year, price, mileage and power are on the canvas. Everything else is in a named group that says how many of its criteria are set, so a form of forty controls reads as six decisions.
requirements.title: The criteria that decide come first

requirements.statement: Each collapsed group carries the number of criteria set within it, so nothing is filtering invisibly.
requirements.title: A closed group says what is inside it

requirements.statement: The add-and-edit sheet was written and never rendered, so Custom search and the Edit button on a non-vehicle bookmark both did nothing at all.
requirements.title: Editing a search that is not a vehicle does something
Waiting looks like waiting
requirements.statement: While markets are answering and nothing has arrived, the screen is blank below the doors: no progress line, no skeleton, nothing but a small count in the header. The render of the loading state shows it.

requirements.title: A failed search does not read as an empty one
requirements.statement: Every market blocked and every market empty draw the same screen: \u201cNo listings found\u201d. The only difference is the Markets door reading \u201c0 ok, 4 not\u201d in small text. Put the reason on the canvas where the absence is.

requirements.title: Say what else was searched for
requirements.statement: A search also covers what each market calls the thing, and the results include offers the typed query never named. The header says how many markets were translated for and nothing says which terms were used, so an unexpected result looks like a mistake rather than the feature working.

states.title: Loading
states.statement: The saved searches have been asked for and have not arrived.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Nothing has been saved yet, so the view carries only the way into a new search.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The server could not be reached, so what is saved cannot be shown.

states.title: Loading
states.statement: The catalogue is being read; the tiles are what stands there meanwhile.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Nothing has been typed, so the categories are the whole of it.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The catalogue could not be read, and the tiles are all that is left.

states.title: Loading
states.statement: Some markets have not answered yet, and what has arrived is shown under a progress line.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Every market answered and none of them carried the thing.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: No market could answer: blocked, timed out, rate limited or erroring.

states.title: Every market answered
states.statement: The search is complete and the list is final until a filter changes.

states.title: Some markets failed
states.statement: A market timed out, was blocked or hit a captcha, so the list is shorter than it should be.

states.title: A market offers its captcha
states.statement: A market answered with a challenge, which can be solved in the crawler's own browser.

states.title: The filters admit none
states.statement: Results exist and the active filters hide all of them, which must read differently from having found nothing.

states.title: Loading
states.statement: The results are still arriving, so there is little yet to narrow.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Nothing has been found, so there is nothing to filter and the controls say so.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: No market answered, so no filter can be built from what came back.

states.title: Loading
states.statement: Markets have been asked and some have not replied.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Every market answered and every one of them was empty.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: Every market failed, each in its own way.

states.title: Cooling down
states.statement: A market is not asked again for a while after a block, so a search that excludes it is not a search that failed.

states.title: Loading
states.statement: Sold listings are being fetched, which is the only part of this that waits.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Nothing sold has been loaded yet, so there is nothing to compare against.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: No market in this search publishes what sold, so the question cannot be answered here.

states.title: Loading
states.statement: The make and model catalogue is being read from the markets themselves.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Nothing has been chosen yet: the form as it opens.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The catalogue could not be read, so make and model fall back to what is bundled.

states.title: Loading
states.statement: Items are being fetched for the area that was set.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Nothing is being given away nearby that has not already been judged.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The server could not be reached, so there is nothing to judge.

states.title: Loading
states.statement: The server's own settings are being read.

states.title: Empty
states.statement: Nothing is configured beyond the defaults.

states.title: Failed
states.statement: The server could not be reached, so its shared settings cannot be shown or changed.

stories.statement:
I want to type what I am after once and have every second-hand market asked, instead of opening
eight sites and searching each of them.
stories.title: Ask every market once

stories.statement:
I want the search to also cover what the market itself calls the thing, because a floor sander is
sold as Parkettschleifmaschine, Parkettschleifer and Parkettschleifgerät and I only thought of one
of them.
stories.title: Find it under a name I did not think of

stories.statement:
I want markets in other countries searched in their own language, because the thing I want is
cheaper in Italy and nobody there advertises it in German.
stories.title: Find it where it is cheap

stories.statement:
I want to pick the exact product from a catalogue when I know it, so the search is not at the mercy
of my spelling.
stories.title: Pick a known product rather than spell it

stories.statement: I want one figure for what the thing goes for, not three competing summaries above the first offer.
stories.title: See what the thing costs

stories.statement:
I want to know where an offer sits against the rest — the median, the spread, and what actually sold
— so I can tell a bargain from a hopeful asking price.
stories.title: Know whether a price is good

stories.statement:
I want to see how far away a thing is and sort by it, because a cheap thing four hundred kilometres
away is not cheap.
stories.title: Know how far it is

stories.statement: I want to see when an ad was posted, because a thing that has sat for three weeks is negotiable.
stories.title: Know how long it has been for sale

stories.statement: I want to block a word and have every offer carrying it disappear, for this search, for good.
stories.title: Never see a word again

stories.statement: I want an offer I have already judged to stop coming back every time I open the search.
stories.title: Dismiss one offer

stories.statement:
I want to change the price band, the markets or the sort order over the results I already have,
without waiting for every market to be asked again.
stories.title: Narrow without starting over

stories.statement: I want to see only what is in the countries I would actually travel to or have shipped.
stories.title: Narrow by country

stories.statement:
I want the price band, the sort order and the condition I chose to still be there when I come back
to the search.
stories.title: Keep what I set

stories.statement: I want to save a search I care about and reopen it, rather than rebuilding it each time.
stories.title: Keep a search

stories.statement:
I want to open a saved search and see what appeared since I last looked, without rereading the whole
list.
stories.title: See what is new since last time

stories.statement:
I want the app to watch a saved search and tell me when something new turns up or something is
priced well under the median.
stories.title: Be told rather than check

stories.statement:
I want to know that a market was blocked rather than empty, because those two look identical today
and one of them means the answer is wrong.
stories.title: Know which markets actually answered

stories.statement:
I want to see the term actually sent to each market, since it is translated per country, and correct
it when the translation is wrong.
stories.title: See what each market was asked

stories.statement:
I want the number of results on screen to mean one thing, not a pre-filter count in the header
disagreeing with a post-filter count on a chip.
stories.title: Trust the count

stories.statement:
I want to say year, mileage, power, gearbox, fuel and body and have each market asked in its own
terms, because a car search on words alone is useless.
stories.title: Describe a vehicle properly

stories.statement:
I want to know that a criterion was applied by the market itself rather than over the first two
pages it happened to return, because only one of those is a real filter.
stories.title: Know which market applied which filter

stories.statement:
I want to describe the ideal vehicle in a sentence and have the list ranked by how well it fits,
beyond what a filter can express.
stories.title: Say what I actually want in words

stories.statement:
I want to be shown things going for nothing near me, one at a time, and have the app learn what I
keep saying yes to.
stories.title: Sift what is given away

Narrow the search without losing your place in the results.
